description: Island kitchens and old trading routes carry Rick through Corsica, Sardinia, Sicily, Puglia, Corfu, Mallorca, Catalonia, Morocco and Turkey, revealing how the Mediterranean links cuisines while preserving fiercely local ingredients and traditions.

s04e01.description: Rick begins among Corsican mountain food, sausages, sheep's cheese and chestnuts before crossing to Sardinia, where coastal cooking and dishes coloured with cuttlefish ink reveal a different island identity.

s04e02.description: Traditional mullet fishing in Sardinia, including techniques with roots in the Roman world, gives way to Palermo and Sicily's vivid street food and pasta culture.

s04e03.description: Catania's fish market anchors the Sicilian leg before Rick crosses to Puglia, where cucina povera turns modest vegetables, bread, pasta and seafood into some of southern Italy's most distinctive food.

s04e04.description: A generous family feast in Corfu introduces Greek island cooking before Rick returns to Mallorca, revisiting the place where he first learned to cook as a young man.

s04e05.description: Mallorcan seafood and roast lamb lead to Barcelona's Boqueria market and Catalan cooking, then south across the Mediterranean toward the spices and communal dishes of Morocco.

s04e06.description: Couscous, tagines and mint tea carry Rick through Morocco before the route ends in south-eastern Turkey, where Silk Road history, kebabs and regional ingredients connect the Mediterranean to Asia.
